package_info.package_name: Imageless Malicious Repository (Downloader/eBook Phishing/Website SEO campaigns)
package_info.why_malicious: These repositories are intentionally created without container images and instead use repository metadata (such as descriptions, READMEs, and tags) to distribute phishing or malware download links. The campaigns exploit Docker Hub’s trust and searchability to lure users into visiting external malicious sites, often at scale, with no legitimate software or container functionality.

execution_context.trigger: When a user browses, searches for, or attempts to pull the repository
execution_context.file_location: Repository metadata fields (description, README, tags) on Docker Hub
required_permissions: network (for user to access external links)
user interaction (clicking on links in metadata)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Repository metadata contains links such as: 'Download eBook here: http://malicious-phishing-site.com' or 'Get the latest software: http://malware-downloader.com'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user browses, searches for, or attempts to pull the repository, the metadata displays external links to phishing or malware sites, the user may click the link, resulting in their browser making a network request to the malicious domain, which can lead to credential theft or malware download.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The repository metadata is used to distribute links to external phishing or malware sites, which is not a legitimate use of Docker Hub repositories. The absence of any container image further indicates the repository's sole purpose is malicious redirection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Docker Hub repositories provide technical details about container images and usage instructions, not unrelated external download or phishing links. The presence of only metadata with no image is highly abnormal.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate repositories may link to official documentation or project homepages, but these are typically to well-known, project-related domains, not to unrelated or suspicious download sites.
key_indicators: Repository has no container image (imageless repository)
Metadata fields (description, README, tags) contain URLs to non-official, suspicious, or blacklisted domains
Descriptions reference eBooks, software downloads, or resources unrelated to the repository's stated purpose
High volume of similarly structured repositories created in a short time frame

attack_chain.action: Malicious actor creates a large number of imageless repositories on Docker Hub, populating metadata fields with enticing links to phishing or malware sites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users discover these repositories via Docker Hub search or browsing.

attack_chain.action: User views the repository metadata and is lured by promises of eBooks, software, or other resources, and clicks on the provided external link.
attack_chain.leads_to: User's browser initiates a network request to the malicious domain.

attack_chain.action: User is redirected to a phishing or malware site, where they may enter credentials or download malicious files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft, malware infection, or further compromise of the user's system or accounts.

behavioral_signatures: Repositories on Docker Hub with no container images but with metadata containing external links
High-volume or automated creation of repositories with similar metadata patterns and external URLs
Repository descriptions or READMEs promising eBooks, software downloads, or unrelated resources
file_indicators: Repositories with empty or missing image layers
README or description fields containing URLs to non-official, suspicious, or blacklisted domains
Metadata fields referencing resources unrelated to container technology
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains listed in repository metadata, such as http://malicious-phishing-site.com or http://malware-downloader.com
User traffic to domains newly associated with Docker Hub repository metadata
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor Docker Hub for repositories lacking container images but containing external links in metadata fields (description, README, tags). Flag and review repositories whose metadata includes URLs to non-official, suspicious, or blacklisted domains. Detect and alert on high-volume or automated creation of such repositories. Monitor user access to these repositories and correlate with outbound network requests to domains found in their metadata. Use domain reputation and blacklist services to validate external links.
